edit.description: chainRefusesPhase takes the shared observational load instead of its own bare catch
the degraded-cost sentence becomes the caller's, so a third surface can name its own
wake/sleep over a chain.ts that loads and throws
the --job read-only suite's job-dir trap gains the assertion that reads it

summary: Route wake/sleep's chain load through loadChainForObservation so a chain that throws is named, not swallowed

per.section: The fix lands at the mechanism

tests: flume wake reports a chain.ts that fails to load instead of proceeding silently
flume sleep reports a chain.ts that fails to load instead of proceeding silently
pins: a job-dir chain.ts is consulted by neither status nor wake nor sleep under --job
acceptance: wake/sleep name a failing chain load on stderr at report parity with status, exit codes unchanged; the --job read-only suite's trap chain now reds the test if it is ever loaded.
notes: src/cliChainLoad.ts:1 claims 'the one best-effort chain load'; src/cli.ts:144 is a second, a bare `catch { return false }` that reports nothing. That silence is also why tests/cliJobResolution.test.ts's 'read-only subcommands ... a job-dir chain.ts is never consulted' plants a trap no assertion reads: status folds a detonation into an exit-0 'hibernating', wake/sleep into nothing at all. Keep the existing no-chain-at-all leg green.
